Hover fly larvae
(Family Syrphidae)
Targeted prey: Aphids, mealybugs and whiteflies.
Description:
Eggs: Small eggs usually deposited on, or near the host insect.
Immatures: Larvae are 'maggots', which are generally white or brownish
in colour or green with two white stripes along the length of the body.
The body tapers towards the head.
Adults: Stout or slender bodied with a large head and eyes. Yellow and
black bands or spots are usually seen on the body. Size: 8–20 mm in
length. A photo of an adult hover fly is shown on page 87.
Biology and predatory activity:
Development from egg to adult takes between 2–6 weeks.
Hover fly larvae are predatory and the adults are pollinators. The
larvae are often seen on plants that are heavily infested with aphids,
mealybugs or whiteflies. Other species of hover fly larvae live in rotting
vegetation. Some larvae are aquatic such as the rat-tailed maggots.
caveat: This source is an Australian (Northern Territory) government field guide, not a Cambodia-specific MAFF publication. It is included as a supplementary international reference for visual identification and general pest/disease biology only. Species presence, seasonal timing (the guide's monthly monitoring calendars reflect the NT dry/wet season cycle), and any pesticide or chemical guidance are specific to northern Australia and may not apply directly to Cambodian conditions, seasons, or registered products. This edition of the source itself does not list specific pesticide products or rates (noted as intentionally omitted pending updated registrations), so none are reported here either.
